title: Best Large Room Dehumidifier (2026): High-Capacity Picks
h1: The Best Large Dehumidifiers for Big Rooms and Open Floor Plans
dek: Great rooms and open-concept spaces have more air to turn over — and people living in them. Here's how to get capacity without the racket.
description: The best large dehumidifier for big rooms in 2026: high-capacity picks for open floor plans, great rooms and finished attics, with pump and quiet options.
intro: A great room, an open kitchen-dining-living space or a finished attic doesn't play by bedroom rules. There's simply more air to move, and the moisture from cooking, showers and a busy household spreads through all of it. A **large dehumidifier** — a high-capacity, 50-pint-class unit with strong airflow — is what it takes to reach the far corners of an open floor plan.

But a big room is also usually a lived-in room, so capacity isn't the only thing that matters. A larger tank (or a pump) saves you from emptying a bucket three times a day, and a reasonable noise level keeps the machine from fighting the TV. Below, we've picked the best large-space dehumidifiers for different needs, from maximum coverage to a quieter option for a living area that's only moderately damp.
topPicksLead: The **Midea Cube 50-Pint** is the best large-room dehumidifier for most homes: strong airflow, a roomy tank in its base and a compact footprint for its capacity.

products.name: Midea Cube 50-Pint Smart Dehumidifier (MAD50S1QWT)
pros: Turbo airflow reaches the corners of open spaces
Large tank built into the base means fewer empties
Compact cube shape for its capacity
products.whyWeLoveIt: In a big open room, a 50-pint unit pulls a lot of water fast — and that's where most dehumidifiers become a chore, because the bucket fills before dinner. The Cube's tank forms its base and holds far more than a typical pull-out bucket, so you can go much longer between trips to the sink.
products.performance: Midea lists 218 CFM of airflow on Turbo and rates the unit for up to 4,500 square feet, with a tank of about 4.35 gallons. It's rated at 50 pints a day under the DOE 2019 test, and you can also attach a hose for continuous drainage. Midea also posts strong predicted-reliability marks in Consumer Reports' brand surveys. It's our top pick in the [best dehumidifier](/best/best-dehumidifier/) roundup too.

products.name: Honeywell 50-Pint Dehumidifier with Pump (TP70PWKNR)
pros: Rated for up to 4,000 square feet
Built-in pump drains up to 15 feet away
Uses a lower-impact refrigerant than its predecessor
cons: Costs more than the Midea Cube
products.whyWeLoveIt: When the room is truly oversized — a finished attic, a vaulted great room, a converted loft — and nowhere near a drain, this Honeywell's coverage rating and pump make sure it isn't undersized or tethered to a bucket.
products.performance: It's sold as a 70-pint unit under the old test standard, which equals a 50-pint rating under the current 2019 DOE procedure. Honeywell rates it for up to 4,000 square feet, and the pump can push water vertically or horizontally up to about 15 feet. The TP70PWKNR is the newer eco-refrigerant version of the long-running TP70PWKN, and both are ENERGY STAR certified. See the rest of the lineup in our [Honeywell dehumidifier guide](/best/best-honeywell-dehumidifier/).

products.whyWeLoveIt: If you want pump convenience without paying top dollar, the HME1003 is the value play. It drains continuously through a hose, so it never needs emptying, and the app is handy in a large multi-use room you're not sitting in all day.
products.performance: It's a 50-pint-class compressor dehumidifier with a built-in pump and app control, and it's also our pick for large or wet spaces in the [basement guide](/best/best-dehumidifier-for-basement/). Owners like setting a humidity target in the app and forgetting about it. Check the pump hose occasionally for kinks — that's the most common reason pump units shut off.

specs.Best for: Large rooms far from a drain

products.whyWeLoveIt: A great room where the TV and the dehumidifier share the same air is where a loud 50-pint machine becomes the thing everyone complains about. If the space is big but only mildly damp, this smaller Frigidaire trades capacity for a noise level you can actually live with.
products.performance: It's rated at 22 pints a day, so it suits a large room with moderate humidity rather than a very damp one. Independent noise measurements put it in the mid-40s decibels on low from about 10 feet away — roughly library-quiet — which is notably lower than many 50-pint units. For more low-noise options, see our [quiet dehumidifier picks](/best/best-quiet-dehumidifier/).

blocks.text: Airflow is the underrated number. Two 50-pint dehumidifiers can cover very different floor areas depending on how much air they move, which is why it's worth checking the CFM figure or coverage rating rather than the pint number alone.

We don't lab-test. We compared capacity under the 2019 DOE test, manufacturer airflow and coverage ratings, tank size and pump options, ENERGY STAR status and warranty terms, and we looked for published, independent noise figures rather than marketing words like "whisper quiet."

We also read owner reviews for patterns that matter in a busy living space: noise complaints, buckets that fill too quickly, pumps that fail and humidity sensors that read far off a separate hygrometer.

sections.heading: What to look for in a large-space dehumidifier

items.label: High capacity, rated the current way
items.text: Look for a 50-pint rating under the 2019 DOE test. Older "70-pint" labels describe the same class of machine. Our [size guide](/guides/dehumidifier-size-guide/) has the full chart.

items.label: Airflow or coverage figure
items.text: A higher CFM rating moves moisture from across an open floor plan to the machine faster.

items.label: Tank size or a pump
items.text: A big room fills a small bucket quickly. A large tank buys time; a pump eliminates emptying altogether. See our [pump picks](/best/best-dehumidifier-with-pump/).

items.label: A real noise number
items.text: If people sit in the room, look for a published decibel figure rather than a "quiet" label.

items.label: Central placement
items.text: One unit can dry a connected open space if it sits centrally with clear airflow. Our [placement guide](/guides/where-to-place-a-dehumidifier/) explains how.

blocks.caption: Capacities under the 2019 DOE test. Use as a starting point, not a rule.

blocks.text: Can one high-capacity dehumidifier dry a whole open floor plan?

Yes, if the area is genuinely connected. Air moves freely across an open kitchen, dining and living space, so one well-placed unit can serve it. It won't reach separate bedrooms behind closed doors down the hall. If you need to dry the whole house, a ducted [whole-house dehumidifier](/best/best-whole-house-dehumidifier/) is the better tool.

items: **Set it to 45–50%.** That's comfortable for people and furniture, and it keeps the compressor from running constantly.
**Use the auto or humidistat mode**, not continuous. Continuous mode in a big room wastes power and can over-dry.
**Run it hardest when the house is empty** — during the workday, for example — and let it cycle down in the evening when you want quiet.
**Clean the filter every two to three weeks** in heavy use. A clogged filter cuts airflow, which matters most in a large space.

The **Midea Cube 50-Pint** is the best large dehumidifier for most big rooms: strong airflow and a tank you won't be emptying constantly. Step up to the **Honeywell TP70PWKNR** for an oversized space far from a drain, choose the **hOmeLabs HME1003** for pump convenience at a lower price, and pick the **Frigidaire FFAD2233W1** when the room is a living space that's only moderately damp and quiet matters most.

faqs.q: What is the best dehumidifier for a large room?
faqs.a: The Midea Cube 50-Pint (MAD50S1QWT). Midea rates it for up to 4,500 square feet with 218 CFM of Turbo airflow, and its large base tank means fewer trips to the sink. For an oversized space far from a drain, the Honeywell TP70PWKNR adds a built-in pump.

faqs.q: What size dehumidifier do I need for a large room?
faqs.a: Under the 2019 DOE standard, a moderately damp room over about 1,000 square feet needs around 35 pints, while a very damp room or one over 2,000 square feet needs 50 pints or more.
Generally, a portable unit rated at 50 pints a day under the current DOE test — the same machines once sold as 70-pint units. Beyond that, you're into commercial or ducted whole-house systems.

faqs.q: Should a large-room dehumidifier have a pump?
faqs.a: It's worth it if the room is far from a sink or drain, or if you want the unit to run for days unattended. In a room you pass through daily, a large tank like the Midea Cube's is often enough.

They're usually louder than small units because they move more air. If the room is a living space, look for a published decibel figure, run the unit on auto rather than continuous, and consider a smaller, quieter model like the Frigidaire FFAD2233W1 if the room is only mildly damp.

faqs.q: Does Hisense make a large room dehumidifier?
faqs.a: Yes, Hisense sells 50-pint models aimed at large rooms, including versions with a built-in pump. Compare their coverage ratings, warranty and noise figures with the picks above before buying.
